title: Mustard greens, fresh, cooked, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Mustard greens (Brassica juncea) are a leafy vegetable from the cruciferous family. Fresh leaves are typically steamed, boiled, or lightly sautéed without added fat to preserve their mild flavor and nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mustard greens are rich in glucosinolates, which convert during cooking into compounds with anti‑inflammatory properties.
In Asian cuisines, mustard greens are commonly used in salads, soups, and as a side dish for rice.
The leaves can range from bright green to a slightly yellow hue depending on growing conditions.
While mustard seeds are a popular spice, the leaves provide a milder, slightly peppery taste.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: One cup of cooked mustard greens supplies over 500 % of the daily value for vitamin K, essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A and carotenoids
items.content: Beta‑carotene in mustard greens is converted to vitamin A, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: Source of vitamin C and antioxidants
items.content: Vitamin C helps combat free radicals and enhances iron absorption from plant foods.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, satiety, and stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: A cup of cooked mustard greens contains about 25 kcal, making it an excellent choice for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Glucosinolates content
items.content: In very large amounts, glucosinolates may cause gastrointestinal irritation in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Thyroid medication interaction
items.content: People taking thyroid medication should consume mustard greens in moderation, as glucosinolates can affect thyroid function.

items.title: Allergy to cruciferous vegetables
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to cruciferous plants.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Steam mustard greens for 3–5 minutes or quickly sauté them without oil to retain nutrients. Add them to salads, soups, omelets, stews, or serve as a side dish with meat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh leaves in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or wrapped in a damp towel for 3–5 days. Cooked mustard greens should be stored in an airtight container in the fridge and used within 2 days.
